title: Potato Biology, Development, Ecology & Evolution — Source Ledger
rule: Sources support botanical and agronomic claims within their documented scope. They do not validate Potatoverse symbolism, theology or Timic deductions; those remain separate interpretations built beside the biology.

sources.source: International Potato Center (CIP), Potato Facts and Figures
sources.notes: CIP describes Solanum tuberosum, Andean origin/domestication, vegetative propagation from tubers and botanical seed production.

sources.source: Potato Genome Sequencing Consortium, Genome sequence and analysis of the tuber crop potato, Nature 475 (2011)
sources.notes: Describes stolons as underground stems that swell into tubers, tubers as storage/vegetative-propagation organs, and common cultivated potato as highly heterozygous and autotetraploid.

sources.source: Physiological and molecular mechanisms associated with potato tuber dormancy, review (2024)
sources.notes: Reviews initiation, maintenance and termination of tuber dormancy and the roles of apical dominance, hormones, cell-cycle regulation and storage conditions.

sources.source: Development of aerial and belowground tubers in potato is governed by photoperiod and epigenetic mechanism (2021)
sources.notes: Reviews molecular, genetic and epigenetic regulation of stolon/tuber fate and integration with photoperiod.

sources.source: Advances in the Modulation of Potato Tuber Dormancy and Sprouting (2024)
sources.notes: Reviews carbohydrate metabolism during dormancy and sprouting, including starch storage, sugar mobilization and the tuber's transition from sink to source.

sources.source: Genome evolution and diversity of wild and cultivated potatoes, Nature 606 (2022)
sources.notes: Provides modern genomic context for wild and cultivated potato diversity and the highly heterozygous tetraploid state of most commercial cultivars.

sources.source: Potato: from functional genomics to genetic improvement (2024), late-blight section
sources.notes: Reviews Phytophthora infestans as the cause of potato late blight, its historical and current crop impact, and resistance/genomic improvement context.

sources.source: International Potato Center, The origins and adaptation of European potatoes reconstructed from historical genomes
sources.notes: Summarizes genomic research tracing Andean origin, vegetative propagation and adaptation after introduction into Europe.

coverage_note: This is a seed provenance ledger for the canonical biology owner, not a complete potato bibliography. Future expansion should add primary experimental sources where the owner makes more specific mechanistic claims.
